P001.text: Act on ordered, dated sequences of door counts, program attendance, survey collection periods and staff workload reports for the two branches, alongside transport schedules and school-term dates.

P002.text: Their disagreement does not establish a timing error: first audit whether they cover comparable periods, opening hours and populations.

P003.text: Uncertain dates, missing reporting intervals and sufficient historical overlap are possibilities to check, not supplied facts.

P004.text: Retain original records and distinguish zero activity from missing data.

P005.text: Before the trial, assemble overlapping historical sequences at the finest common reliable time resolution, retaining weekday/weekend distinctions and normalizing activity for actual opening hours.

P006.text: Anchor the timeline with verified dates.

P007.text: Compare ordered changes across records around several distinctive events, such as term transitions or transport changes; shift only records whose calendar placement is genuinely uncertain, within documented plausible bounds.

P008.text: Accept a proposed alignment only if it repeatedly fits independent anchors and overlapping records, rather than one attractive match.

P009.text: Flag possible missing, duplicated or misassigned intervals for verification against original logs; leave unresolved periods uncertain.

P010.text: Do not shift securely dated evidence to eliminate disagreement.

P011.text: Then specify a reversible three-month weekday-to-weekend transfer at the two branches, conditional on a roster demonstrating compliance with the existing staffing budget.

P012.text: Before launch, set explicit numerical criteria for meaningful access gains, acceptable weekday losses, workload and service reliability; identify who reviews them and when.

P013.text: Preserve the original schedule for restoration, monitor weekly and conduct a midpoint review.

P014.text: Where available, use unchanged branches and comparable historical periods to check seasonal influences.

P015.text: Look for a candidate alignment that produces repeated correspondence in the timing and order of distinctive changes across independently anchored records, including overlaps not used to choose it.

P016.text: Different measures need not have matching magnitudes or directions; any expected correspondence must have a stated reason.

P017.text: An unexplained gap or duplicated interval would prompt a source-log check, not automatic correction.

P018.text: During the trial, observe weekend use, total weekly use, displaced weekday access, reports of previously unmet needs, workload, staffing costs and service failures on the checked timeline, marking term and transport changes.

P019.text: These are proposed observations, not established results.

P020.text: Repeated, independently checked temporal matches would support assigning uncertain records to particular periods and checking or extending the shared timeline through genuine overlaps.

P021.text: This would make disagreements more interpretable: evidence may concern different periods, or may remain substantively different after alignment.

P022.text: Alignment alone would not demonstrate unmet demand or a causal benefit from weekend opening.

P023.text: At the midpoint and end, use the aligned evidence and predeclared criteria to recommend keeping the schedule if access gains meet the threshold while weekday losses, workload and costs remain acceptable; changing the allocation if benefits are concentrated in particular hours or branches; or restoring the original schedule if benefits fall short or harms exceed limits.

P024.text: Any continuation would require a separate decision beyond the three-month trial.

P025.text: Branch-specific events, weak shared seasonal effects, repetitive weekly patterns, reporting errors, faulty date anchors and insufficient overlap can create false or ambiguous alignments.

P026.text: Survey responses, attendance, door counts and workload measure different things and may share collection biases, so agreement is not automatically independent confirmation.

P027.text: If several alignments remain plausible, stop assigning exact dates and report how each affects the decision.

P028.text: A three-month trial cannot reproduce distinctive multi-year matching or establish year-round demand; seek longer historical overlap where available and label unsupported seasonal extrapolation uncertain.

P029.text: Pause or reverse the trial if budget compliance, safe staffing or essential service cannot be maintained.

P030.text: If evidence remains inadequate at expiry, restore the prior schedule pending a separately authorized extension with a specified evidence gap and review date; do not treat uncertainty as proof of success or failure.
